title: Conventional Commits Best Practices
description: A comprehensive guide to implementing conventional commits for effective Git versioning

versioning_principles.description: Follow semantic versioning (SemVer) principles with MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format

commit_types.description: A code change that improves performance
Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code
A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies
Changes to CI configuration files and scripts
Other changes that don't modify src or test files

type.description: The type of change being made
validation: Should be one of the standard types

scope.description: The part of the codebase affected

description.description: A short summary of the change

body.description: A longer description of the change
body.format: separated by a blank line from the description
validation: Must include motivation for the change
Must include contrasts with previous behavior

footer.format: Include breaking changes or issue references

indication: Prefix with '!' after type (e.g., feat!: breaking change)
breaking_changes.format:
BREAKING CHANGE: <description of breaking change>

<details of the breaking change>
breaking_changes.example:
feat!: remove deprecated login method

BREAKING CHANGE: The old login method has been removed.
  This affects users who were still using the old authentication flow.

best_practices.advice: Write commit messages that clearly explain the intent of the change
Make focused commits that address one issue at a time
Maintain consistent formatting across all commits in the repository
Ensure each commit type accurately reflects the nature of the changes
Use scope consistently to indicate which part of the codebase was modified
Include test changes in the same commit as the code changes they test

common_mistakes_to_avoid.better: fix(auth): resolve null pointer in login validation
